name: a-fog-swallowed-park
idea: Beat A, 1919. An extreme wide from a little above: a park drowned in thick, low-lying grey fog at dawn, drawn in pen and grey ink wash on yellowed newsprint, the far trees and railings fading out within a few metres. The bench is the only solid thing. The fat, top-hatted rich man is a dark mass slightly too big for it, the crown of his hat dissolving into the fog, and he lifts one gloved hand in a lazy wave-off. The one-legged soldier with his crutch is small and pale at the other end, half gone into the mist. The top third is open fog for a caption.

name: a-gaslamp-silent-film-still
idea: Beat A, 1919, done as a single frame of a silent horror film rather than a cartoon: orthochromatic nitrate look, chalk-white skin, crushed blacks with no mid-grey, heavy silver grain, scratches and an iris vignette. Night; a single gas lamp hangs right above the bench, so the hard top light turns the rich man's eye sockets into black pits under the hat brim while his polite smile glows white. Medium two-shot at eye level: he waves the soldier off with a limp hand; the soldier, crutch across his knee, is mostly in shadow. The darkness above the lamp leaves room for a caption.

name: a-his-shadow-arrives-first
idea: Beat A, 1919, an expressionist woodcut or linocut in rust-orange and black with gouged, jagged lines. The camera is on the ground beside the tip of the soldier's crutch, looking along the gravel path. A low dusk sun behind the bench throws the rich man's shadow huge and stretched, tall top hat and fat body bent across the path and up over the seated soldier. The man himself sits small and sharp at the top of the frame, mid wave-off. The canted angle and the wrong-sized shadow carry the dread; the sky above holds the caption.

name: b-blurred-behind-the-nurse
idea: Beat B, today, photographic and cinematic rather than drawn. Night, a sodium-orange streetlamp, fine drizzle mist, and the same bench rusted, its green paint peeling. In the foreground, pin-sharp, a nurse in scrubs slumps at one end, eyes shut, lanyard twisted, utterly spent. Behind and beside her, thrown out of focus by a shallow depth of field, the fat top-hatted man sits on the same bench, a blurred dark bulk with a pale smile and one raised hand waving her off; the eye has to strain to read him. The dark wet sky gives the caption room.

name: b-crosshatched-grin-closeup
idea: Beat B, today. An extreme close-up of the rich man's face filling the 9:16 frame edge to edge, with no background, in obsessive black-ink crosshatching and stippling on white paper. The hat brim cuts across the top; the eye sockets are hatched near-black and the smile is far too wide and polite. In the wet shine of one eye sits the only other figure: a tiny exhausted nurse in scrubs on the bench, seen as his reflection. White space is left low on the frame below the jowls for a caption. Pure horror-manga ink pressure on an editorial-cartoon fat cat.

name: b-low-poly-short-draw-distance
idea: Beat B, today, in the look of a late-1990s console survival-horror game: low-poly 3D, warping blurry textures, dithered colour gradients, and fog so close that the park ends a few metres past the bench. A fixed high corner camera looks down like a security angle. The nurse in scrubs sits in a small cold pool of light, rendered in the same crude low-poly as everything else; the rich man beside her in top hat and frock coat is the one thing drawn in crisp, high detail, his hand half raised in a wave-off, which makes him wrong. Greenish-grey 4 a.m. palette, with the fog at the top for the caption.

name: c-black-painting-on-plaster
idea: Beat C, the button. Oil smeared onto a cracked plaster wall, the palette held to ochre, brown, grey and black, with a single white in his shirt front. The rich man, the same fat top-hatted figure, is pushed hard to one side of the frame and crouches forward on the bench in the dark, enormous, grinning, his hand raised in that same lazy wave-off. The rest of the frame is heavy empty darkness where the bench fades out, so it reads as if he alone has outlived the painting. The empty upper area takes the caption.

name: c-the-only-still-thing
idea: Beat C, the button. An old glass-plate studio photograph, silver-grey, with mercury bloom, scratches and chipped corners, taken as a very long exposure in daylight. The fat top-hatted rich man sits frontal and full-figure on the bench, perfectly sharp and smiling, one hand lifted in the wave. Everything around him has smeared into ghost streaks over the exposure: passers-by, soldiers, nurses, crowds and leaves are blurred to transparency because they moved and aged, and he alone stayed still and sharp. Pale washed-out sky above for the caption.

name: c-rust-dust-wasteland
idea: Beat C, the button. An extreme wide of a park that is gone: a dust-choked, ochre-and-rust wasteland at a brown noon, rusted railings bent over, a dead tree, a lamp post collapsed into ash, painted in a dense dystopian surrealist manner with a palette held to three or four related tones. Dead centre and small, the bench is intact, and on it the fat top-hatted man sits immaculate, clean and unaged, the one light accent in the frame, waving off nobody, because nobody is left. The dust sky above holds the caption.
